greet.text: "Lead on. I'll keep an eye on your back, and the other one on the trees."

choices.text: Your father's story, about who founded Riverwatch. Is it true?
I read the roll in the barrow.
Go home. I'll find you later.

warm.text: He grins. "Where to, then? Wherever it is, I'd rather be there with you than at the stones with the captain."

choices.text: Your father's story, about who founded Riverwatch. Is it true?
I read the roll in the barrow.
Go home. I'll find you later.

cold.text: "What." Not a question. He doesn't quite look at you.

choices.text: Your father's story, about who founded Riverwatch. Is it true?
I read the roll in the barrow.
Go home. I'll find you later.

wait.text: "I'll be here. Don't make me come looking."

home.text: "Back to the stones, then. The captain will be thrilled."

founded.text: "True? It's a story. One of Hallam's own hunters held the ford, and was given the land for it, and his company with him." He scratches his jaw. "There's a roll of their names in the old barrow, in a niche by the door. My father went to read it once, and came back and never talked about it. I've never had the nerve."

choices.text: Then let's go and read it.

founded_go.text: "The barrow's south-west of the stones. Bring a torch. And if it's nothing, you never saw me nervous."

roll.text: "Well?" He's trying to sound like he doesn't care. "What does it say?"

choices.text: The truth: they hunted the lights, and were paid in land for it. Your family's on it.
Just names. Old soldiers, and what they were given.

roll_truth.text: He takes the roll and reads it twice. "Aldo Brannoch. Twenty-two lights." He rolls it up very carefully. "'The lights asked for mercy in their own tongue.'" A long breath. "I was raised on that song. Hallam and his hook. I sang it to my sister." He hands it back. "Thank you for not lying to me. I'm going to need to think about what I'm guarding."

roll_lie.text: "Names." He looks at you a moment too long. "Right. Good. That's... good." He doesn't ask to see it.
